subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The resolution of an electron microscope is greater than that of a light microscope because:
options: electrons have a much shorter wavelength than visible light
electrons have a longer wavelength than light
the specimen is stained more heavily
electrons travel more slowly than light
questions.explain: Resolution depends on wavelength; the very short wavelength of an electron beam allows much finer detail to be distinguished.

questions.q: A feature found in some prokaryotic cells but never in eukaryotic cells is:
questions.explain: Plasmids, small circular loops of DNA separate from the main chromosome, are characteristic of prokaryotes and absent from eukaryotic cells.

questions.q: In the formation of a phosphodiester bond between two nucleotides, the bond forms between:
options: the base of one nucleotide and the sugar of the next
the phosphate group of one nucleotide and the deoxyribose of the adjacent nucleotide
questions.explain: A condensation reaction links the phosphate of one nucleotide to the sugar of the next, forming the sugar-phosphate backbone.

questions.q: A low Km value for an enzyme indicates that the enzyme:
options: has a low affinity for its substrate
reaches half its maximum rate at a low substrate concentration, indicating high affinity
questions.explain: If half-maximal rate is reached at low substrate concentration, the enzyme binds substrate readily, so a low Km means high affinity.

questions.q: Why does a high density of mitochondria near a cell-surface membrane suggest the cell carries out a lot of active transport?
options: mitochondria supply the ATP required to power carrier proteins against the concentration gradient
questions.explain: Active transport needs ATP, so many mitochondria close to the membrane indicate a high demand for energy to drive pumping.

questions.q: A property of water that makes it an effective coolant in transpiration and sweating is its:
options: inability to act as a solvent
questions.explain: Water's high latent heat of vaporisation means much heat energy is removed when it evaporates, providing efficient cooling.

questions.q: Active transport is inhibited by a respiratory poison such as cyanide because:
options: the poison denatures the phospholipid bilayer
it prevents ATP production, removing the energy needed to pump substances against their gradient
questions.explain: Active transport depends on ATP from aerobic respiration; inhibiting respiration removes the energy source, halting the pumping of substances against their gradient.

questions.q: The fluid-mosaic model describes the cell membrane as:
options: a fluid phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in a mosaic pattern
a continuous protein sheet with no lipid
a rigid layer of protein sandwiched between lipid
questions.explain: The model depicts a fluid bilayer in which proteins are scattered like a mosaic and can move laterally within the membrane.

questions.q: Why does the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction typically decrease over time when measured as product formed?
options: Substrate concentration falls as it is converted to product, reducing collision frequency
The enzyme is denatured by the product
The activation energy increases over time
questions.explain: As substrate is depleted, fewer enzyme-substrate complexes form per unit time, so the rate declines until substrate runs out.

questions.q: A plant cell with a water potential of -500 kPa is placed in a solution of water potential -300 kPa. The cell will:
options: gain water by osmosis because the solution has a higher (less negative) water potential
questions.explain: Water moves from higher to lower water potential, so water enters the cell (from -300 to -500), and the cell gains water and becomes more turgid.

questions.q: During which stage of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles?
questions.explain: In anaphase the centromeres divide and spindle fibres pull the sister chromatids to opposite poles of the cell.

questions.q: Cells specialised for absorption, such as the epithelial cells of the ileum, increase their rate of uptake by having:
options: microvilli that greatly increase the surface area of the membrane for transport proteins
fewer carrier proteins to reduce competition
questions.explain: Microvilli increase the membrane surface area, providing more sites for carrier and co-transport proteins and so faster absorption.

questions.q: A phospholipid differs from a triglyceride in that a phospholipid has:
options: only ester bonds and no hydrophilic region
three fatty acids attached to glycerol
one fatty acid replaced by a phosphate-containing hydrophilic group
questions.explain: In a phospholipid, one of the three fatty acids of a triglyceride is replaced by a hydrophilic phosphate group, making the molecule amphipathic.

questions.q: Glycogen and amylose both store glucose, but glycogen is more highly branched. A direct consequence of this branching is that glycogen:
options: forms straight chains that pack into fibres
can be hydrolysed more rapidly because of more terminal glucose residues
questions.explain: More branch points give more free ends from which glucose can be released quickly, suiting the high metabolic rate of animals.

questions.q: The function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is to:
options: synthesise proteins via attached ribosomes and transport them
questions.explain: The RER is studded with ribosomes that synthesise proteins, which are folded and transported through its cisternae.

questions.q: Why can a light microscope not resolve two ribosomes that are 25 nm apart?
options: light has too short a wavelength
the resolving power of a light microscope (about 200 nm) is limited by the wavelength of visible light, which is far larger than 25 nm
ribosomes are too large to be seen
questions.explain: Visible light's wavelength limits resolution to roughly 200 nm, so structures only 25 nm apart cannot be distinguished by a light microscope.

questions.q: A cell with a diploid number of 8 (2n=8) undergoing meiosis will produce gametes containing how many chromosomes, and how many distinct combinations are possible from independent assortment alone?
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid (n=4), and with 4 homologous pairs independent assortment gives 2 to the power 4 = 16 possible chromosome combinations.

questions.q: When a fully turgid plant cell has its pressure potential exactly balancing its solute potential, its water potential is zero, meaning:
options: there is no net movement of water into or out of the cell when surrounded by pure water
questions.explain: At full turgor the inward pressure potential equals the solute potential in magnitude, giving Psi = 0, so no net water movement occurs with pure water outside.

questions.q: A red blood cell placed in pure water bursts (haemolysis) because:
options: water enters down a water potential gradient and the cell has no rigid wall to resist swelling
solutes enter the cell by active transport
water leaves the cell by osmosis
the membrane actively pumps water in
questions.explain: Pure water has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm, so water enters by osmosis; lacking a cell wall, the animal cell swells and lyses.

questions.q: The secondary structure of a protein (alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet) is stabilised primarily by:
options: hydrogen bonds between the C=O and N-H groups of the backbone
questions.explain: Secondary structure arises from regular hydrogen bonding between backbone carbonyl and amine groups, independent of R-group identity.

questions.q: In which stage of mitosis do chromosomes align along the equator (metaphase plate)?
questions.explain: During metaphase, chromosomes line up at the cell equator attached to spindle fibres by their centromeres.

questions.q: Why is glycogen a more suitable storage molecule than cellulose in animal cells?
options: It is highly branched, giving many free ends for rapid hydrolysis
Its glycosidic bonds cannot be hydrolysed
It contains beta-glucose, which is more soluble
It is unbranched and so packs tightly into fibres
questions.explain: Glycogen's highly branched structure provides many terminal glucose units, allowing rapid enzymatic release of glucose to meet metabolic demand.

questions.q: Meiosis generates genetic variation partly through independent assortment, which occurs because:
options: homologous chromosomes exchange alleles by crossing over
maternal and paternal chromosomes orient randomly at the metaphase plate, so combinations in gametes vary
questions.explain: The random orientation of homologous pairs in metaphase I means each gamete receives a different mix of maternal and paternal chromosomes.

questions.q: Bulk transport of large quantities of material out of a cell by vesicles fusing with the membrane is called:
questions.explain: Exocytosis is the energy-requiring process in which vesicles fuse with the cell-surface membrane to release their contents outside the cell.

questions.q: The Golgi apparatus is mainly responsible for:
options: modifying, packaging and sorting proteins into vesicles for secretion
questions.explain: The Golgi modifies proteins (e.g. adding carbohydrate), packages them into vesicles and labels them for their destination.

questions.q: A competitive inhibitor characteristically increases the apparent Km of an enzyme while leaving Vmax unchanged because it:
options: binds permanently to the active site
competes with substrate for the active site, so more substrate is needed to reach the same rate
questions.explain: Competition for the active site means a higher substrate concentration is required for half-maximal rate (higher Km), but saturating substrate still achieves Vmax.

questions.q: The water potential of pure water at standard temperature and pressure is:
options: equal to the solute potential of the cell
questions.explain: Pure water has the highest water potential, defined as 0 kPa; adding solute makes the water potential more negative.

questions.q: In differential centrifugation of a cell homogenate, the order in which organelles sediment as speed increases is:
options: all organelles sediment together at the same speed
ribosomes first because they are densest
nuclei, then mitochondria/chloroplasts, then endoplasmic reticulum, then ribosomes
questions.explain: The densest, largest organelles (nuclei) sediment first at low speeds; progressively smaller, less dense organelles pellet at higher speeds, with ribosomes last.

questions.q: ATP is resynthesised from ADP and inorganic phosphate in a reaction that is:
options: a spontaneous exergonic process needing no enzyme
a condensation requiring energy, catalysed by ATP synthase
questions.explain: Phosphorylation of ADP is an endergonic condensation reaction catalysed by ATP synthase, storing energy in the new phosphate bond.

questions.q: When the difference in concentration of a freely diffusing molecule across a membrane is doubled, the rate of simple diffusion will:
options: approximately double, because rate is proportional to the concentration gradient
questions.explain: For simple diffusion across a membrane, rate is proportional to the steepness of the concentration gradient, so doubling the gradient roughly doubles the rate.
